events.title: Robert the Bruce Crowned King of Scots
events.description: At Scone, Robert the Bruce was crowned King of Scotland. He took the throne in the middle of a bitter struggle against English domination and in the shadow of a civil conflict among Scottish nobles.
events.significance: His reign became the centrepiece of Scotland's Wars of Independence. It ultimately led to the recognition of Scottish sovereignty.

events.title: Christiaan Huygens Discovers Titan
events.description: The Dutch scientist Christiaan Huygens spotted a faint point of light circling Saturn. It was the planet's largest moon, later named Titan.
events.significance: It was the first moon found orbiting Saturn. Centuries later, Titan became a prime target for space exploration because of its thick atmosphere.

events.title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
events.description: A fire tore through the Triangle Shirtwaist Company in New York City and killed 146 garment workers, many of them young immigrant women. Locked exits and inadequate safety measures contributed to the death toll.
events.significance: The tragedy fueled the labor movement and led to sweeping workplace safety and fire-code reforms in the United States.

events.title: Birth of Aretha Franklin
events.description: Aretha Franklin, the future Queen of Soul, was born. She rose from gospel roots to become one of the most powerful voices in American music.
events.significance: Her recordings and her anthems of empowerment made her a cultural icon, and she was among the most celebrated singers of the 20th century.

events.title: Treaty of Rome Founds the European Economic Community
events.description: Six European countries signed the Treaty of Rome and created the European Economic Community. The aim was to build a common market and closer economic cooperation after World War II.
events.significance: The treaty laid the groundwork for what grew into the European Union.
